messages:
Elaine: morning — quick kernel roundtable. quick status blast: what shipped, any blockers, any small asks for reviews. keeping this short so on-call can follow.
Noah: shipped micro-batcher tuning yesterday. throughput +12% on our microbench for 2-4k seqs. will push perf logs in a sec.
Maya: canary rolled for batcher-heuristic tweak (optimize slot packing). seeing ~40ms tail increase for 8k sequences on two hosts. investigating; might be a slot contention edge.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded: commit 9f3b2a7 -> batcher-heuristic. 3 hosts, 5m observation window.
Derek: where are the perf logs? can you paste the bench command and flamegraph link?
Noah: logs: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-ops/bench/1798765432/noah-microbatch-2026-03-16.tar.gz
Noah: reproduce cmd: `./bench/run.sh --model=redwood-13B --seq=4096 --concurrency=48 --iters=300`
Noah: flamegraph: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/1798765432 (public to eng-runtime)
Maya: KV warmup note: on cold starts we're seeing evictions that spike cold p99 to ~5s. root cause looks like prefetcher racing with the eviction pruner on startup. filed PR #4523 with a small lock around warmup.
Elaine: linking PR: https://git.redwood/company/infra/pull/4523 — @Noah can you glance at the locking approach? I'm wary of introducing a global stall.
Noah: will review now. initial glance: locking window is tiny, but we should avoid blocking request paths. propose `prefetcher.try_lock()` + hop backoff instead of full blocker. comment incoming.
Tia: on-call heads up: if canary >2% p99 tail regress, I'll trigger rollback. I also noticed autoscaler rule `batcher_scale_down_delay` is 30s; that's aggressive for cold-warm interactions. can we set to 90s for canary hosts?
Maya: noted — updating canary config to `batcher_scale_down_delay=90s` and re-running canary. will post results in ~10m.
Derek: quick ask — can someone post a diff of the heuristic change? small patch would help code review.
Maya: diff paste:```diff
@@ -112,7 +112,11 @@
- func pickSlot(req) { return bestFit(req) }
+ func pickSlot(req) {
+   // prefer packing smaller trailing sequences to reduce tail
+   if req.seq > 2048 { return conservativeFit(req) }
+   return bestFit(req)
+ }
```
Elaine: thanks. small comment: add a unit test for pickSlot with edge-case sequences >8192.
Noah: reviewed PR #4523 and left two inline comments (avoid global mutex; drop backoff jitter).
Maya: thanks both — will push a follow-up patch today.
deploy-bot: Canary metrics updated: p50 +2ms, p95 +8ms, p99 +42ms (8k seqs), throughput +11% (2-4k seqs). no error rate change.
Tia: holding until follow-up patch lands. if Maya's patch fixes cold evictions, we can promote.
Derek: I'll pair-review the heuristic diff after lunch. otherwise :thumbsup:.
Elaine: ok — plan: Maya will push fixes, Noah to re-run microbench, Derek to review heuristic, Tia to watch canary. post updates here.
Noah: re-run queued; ETA ~25m.
Maya: pushing hotfix now (small backoff, remove global lock). will update when canary completes.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded: commit a1d4f6b -> batcher-heuristic-hotfix. 3 hosts, 5m window.
Maya: canary metrics after hotfix: p99 back to baseline (~+5ms) and throughput still +9%. looks good.
Tia: rolling to stable in 30m if no regressions. I'll post rollback note if anything spikes.
Derek: thanks team, will follow up on the review later.
Elaine: perfect — short check-in done. if anything critical ping #incidents. :coffee:
